rows.citation: Andrew G. Clark, Michael Foster, Benedikt Prifling, et al. (2023). Testing Causality in Scientific Modelling Software. ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology, 33(1), 1-42.
rows.model_type: scientific simulation models: Poisson line tessellation, Luo-Rudy 1991 cardiac action potential ODE model, Covasim agent-based epidemic model
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no mutation analysis or seeded-fault evaluation found in accepted manuscript text; faults found were real (e.g. a reported Covasim issue).
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - tests effects of input interventions (e.g. six LR91 conductances) via metamorphic relations, not a current-clamp protocol battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - LR91 case study uses cardiac APD90 as output; no neural/eFEL features or multi-feature fingerprints.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - reduces model executions by inferring outcomes from existing data via causal inference; no test or protocol subset selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - three evaluative case studies replicating prior studies; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Infers metamorphic outcomes from causal DAGs and reused data, including a cardiac AP model. NeuroSem instead uses mutants, stimulus batteries, calibrated tolerances and greedy selection with held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works API (7 authors, TOSEM 33(1):1-42); OpenAlex W4384030289 (abstract); Semantic Scholar (arXiv 2209.00357, open PDF); accepted manuscript text read (White Rose eprints 200672); GitHub REST API for repo and licence.
